editorial:
You follow Mick Haller, a smooth defense lawyer who works from his Lincoln Continental. He usually handles small-time crooks, but a rich Beverly Hills client accused of attempted murder promises a huge payday. At first it looks easy, but the case turns dark and dangerous. The movie feels like a smart, gritty courtroom thriller with street-level charm and steady tension. You will like the mix of courtroom talk and streetwise humor.

Matthew McConaughey gives a confident, likable performance, and the supporting cast keeps things lively. The pacing stays brisk, with twists that keep you guessing without getting confusing. It can feel a little familiar if you have seen many legal thrillers, and some side plots get rushed. Still, it is a fun, satisfying watch for fans of crime dramas. The story moves fast enough that you never feel bored. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mick realizes Louis Roulet is guilty of both the assault and an earlier murder. Because of lawyer rules, Mick cannot simply tell police, so he uses the trial and his own safety to force the truth out. Roulet is arrested for the old murder, Jesus Martinez is freed, and Mick survives Roulet's attack. Mick walks away shaken but still working, now more careful about which clients he takes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves courtroom thrillers and crime dramas.
